extracted.intended_audience: cognitive neuroscience / neuroimaging researchers studying laughter, social communication, and autism
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, running, and reporting an event-related fMRI experiment that compares neural and behavioral responses to spontaneous vs conversational laughter in autistic and non-autistic adults, including stimulus creation/validation, acquisition, preprocessing, statistical modeling, and ROI analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant inclusion and matching
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants were right-handed and had no speech, hearing or neurological difficulties. Groups were matched/comparable for sex, age, verbal, performance, and full-scale IQ; groups differed on Autism Spectrum Quotient (AQ). Autistic participants had received an official diagnosis from a qualified clinician. Non-autistic participants with an AQ score below the cut-off of 32 were included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report group comparability statistics (χ2, t-tests), state diagnostic verification method; if ADOS could not be administered, report alternative screening (AQ) and recruitment sources (disability services, autism databases). Document exclusions (e.g., participants unable to complete scan) and reassess group comparability after exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Informed written consent was obtained prior to testing, and the project received approval from the university research ethics committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state ethics approval and consent process in methods. Note recruitment channels and any pandemic-related testing restrictions that affected procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word stimulus selection to avoid floor/ceiling effects
rubrics_metrics.description: A subset of 300 words was selected from an original pool; words were chosen to avoid floor and ceiling effects per baseline ratings (funniness mean=3.309, SD=0.586; intelligibility mean=92.959%, SD=10.619%). Initially selected 719 words with a humor rating higher than 2.8 from Engelthaler & Hills (2018) pool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-screen large pools using established norms; choose thresholds (e.g., humor rating >2.8) to avoid floor/ceiling; obtain baseline ratings from independent participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human screening of stimulus appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of 621 words was screened by four native English speakers to ensure appropriateness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have multiple native speakers review candidate stimuli for appropriateness and comprehension before final selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline behavioral norming and list matching
rubrics_metrics.description: An online baseline ratings task with 58 native English speakers rated funniness and understanding; 621 words assigned to three lists matched on original humor ratings (List means ~3.19-3.20).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use independent online norming to produce matched lists; random assignment of raters to lists; report list matching statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional recording and acoustic editing of word stimuli
rubrics_metrics.description: Words were recorded by a professional male comedian reading in a comedic manner; raw audio downsampled to 44,100 Hz to mono .wav, 32-bit, trimmed/edited into 1-s files using Audacity, normalized for RMS amplitude using PRAAT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent professional recordings, downsample and standardize file format and bit-depth, trim to fixed duration, and perform RMS normalization with documented tools (Audacity, PRAAT). Report duration, RMS, and pitch statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laughter and NV stimuli creation and validation
rubrics_metrics.description: 150 sound stimuli: 50 spontaneous laughter, 50 conversational laughter recorded using previously validated methods (McGettigan et al. 2015) and selected from prior study; 50 noise-vocoded (NV) human vocalizations created by one-channel noise-vocoding of various emotional vocalizations to remove emotional meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use validated elicitation/recording methods for laughter types, document sources and selection procedures. Create NV controls via established noise-vocoding methods and confirm they lack recognizable emotional meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acoustic normalization and comparability checks
rubrics_metrics.description: All stimuli were normalized for RMS amplitude using PRAAT; acoustic parameters extracted; one-way ANOVA indicated spontaneous laughter, conversational laughter and NV stimuli were comparable in duration, RMS, and intensity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalize RMS for all stimuli; extract and report acoustic measures (duration, RMS, intensity); statistically test and report comparability (ANOVA) across conditions; include supplementary tables for detailed acoustic comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event-related fMRI experimental design parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Event-related paradigm: jittered ITI 2–4 s; fixed ISI 0.09 s between word and sound; rest condition = 2 s silence after ITI; vigilance trials with 0.5 s beep requiring button press within 3 s; four functional runs (~14 min each) with 25 trials per condition and five vigilance trials per run; each functional run ~105 trials; sound stimuli used twice; trial pseudorandomization prevented >2 consecutive same-condition trials; rest/vigilance not first or consecutive; pairs pseudorandomized and counterbalanced across runs and participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify ITI/ISI durations, number of runs, trials per condition, vigilance checks, and pseudorandomization/counterbalancing rules to avoid order effects; report use of rest/vigilance placement constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant instructions and intentional blinding
rubrics_metrics.description: Participants were informed the fMRI study was about humor processing; any mention of laughter was intentionally avoided during recruitment and prior to testing; they were told to listen to humorous words and people's reactions and press a button when they heard a beep.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design participant instructions to avoid priming specific stimulus features under investigation (e.g., do not mention 'laughter' if studying implicit laughter processing). Provide practice trials to check understanding and volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-scan behavioral rating task parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-scan, participants listened to word-plus-laughter pairs again and rated funniness on a 7-point scale ('How funny was the word the way that Ben said it?'); up to 6 s per trial; practice session before task; due to COVID restrictions NV pairs excluded; task lasted ~25 min.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use consistent rating scales (7-point), time limits per trial, and practice trials. Document any deviations (e.g., exclusions due to time constraints) and how they affect analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: fMRI acquisition hardware and sequence parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuous event-related fMRI on Siemens Avanto 1.5-Tesla MRI scanner with 32-channel head coil; four runs of 260 echo-planar whole-brain volumes (TR=3 s; TE=50 ms; TA=86 ms; slice tilt =25° ±5°; flip angle=90°; 3 mm × 3 mm × 3 mm in-plane resolution). High-resolution T1-weighted anatomical: 176 sagittal slices, TR=2730 ms; TE=3.57 ms; flip angle=7°; acquisition matrix=224×256×176; slice thickness 1 mm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report scanner model, coil, EPI parameters (TR, TE, TA, flip angle, slice tilt, voxel size), number of volumes/runs, and anatomical scan parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: fMRI preprocessing pipeline and order
rubrics_metrics.description: Discard first three volumes; spatial alignment along AC-PC; slice time correction using last slice as reference; spatial realignment and registration to mean; structural co-registration; segmentation with SPM12 tissue probability maps; use forward deformation to normalize to standard MNI space; resample normalized functional images to 2×2×2 mm voxels; spatial smoothing with isotropic 8 mm FWHM Gaussian kernel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe preprocessing steps in order, including volume discard, slice-timing reference, realignment, coregistration, segmentation-based normalization, target voxel size, and smoothing kernel size. Name software and versions (e.g., SPM12, MATLAB R2018B).

rubrics_metrics.name: First-level GLM design and nuisance regressors
rubrics_metrics.description: Voxelwise general linear model with regressors for onsets/durations of (1) words plus spontaneous laughter, (2) words plus conversational laughter, (3) words plus NV stimuli, and (4) vigilance trials; plus six realignment parameter regressors as nuisance; data high-pass filtered at 128 s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model each experimental condition explicitly, include motion regressors, and apply a suitable high-pass filter (128 s). Report model construction and temporal filtering choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specified contrasts for individual and group analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual contrasts were All Laughs (Spont Laugh & Conver Laugh) > NV, Spont Laugh > NV, Conver Laugh > NV; these contrasts across four runs were entered into second-level two-sample t-test for group analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define relevant first-level contrasts and the second-level design (e.g., two-sample t-tests comparing groups). Include movement parameters as nuisance variables at group level as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple comparisons correction approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Whole-brain analysis results were corrected using a cluster-extent-based thresholding approach: voxel-wise threshold of P<0.001 combined with a cluster extent threshold determined by SPM12 with P<0.05 family-wise-error cluster-corrected threshold. All reported clusters exceeded this cluster-corrected threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State voxelwise height threshold and cluster FWE correction criterion; justify thresholding approach and report that all reported clusters survive correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting conventions for coordinates and anatomical labels
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported cluster coordinates correspond to the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI) coordinate system and were labeled using the AAL labelling atlas in SPM12.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify coordinate space (MNI), labeling atlas (AAL), and software used for labeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: A priori ROI definition and independence
rubrics_metrics.description: A priori ROIs taken from MNI peak coordinates from a prior fMRI study (McGettigan et al. 2015): left superior medial frontal gyrus (mPFC; x=−3,y=54,z=9), left temporal thalamus (x=−3,y=−6,z=9), and right ACC (x=0,y=30,z=30). ROIs created as spherical 8-mm radius using MarsBaR. An independent meta-analytic mPFC ROI (x=0,y=50,z=20) from Van Overwalle & Baetens (2009) was also used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define ROIs from independent prior literature to avoid circularity. Build spherical ROIs with specified radius (8 mm) and extraction method (MarsBaR), and justify ROI coordinates with citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of circular analysis ('double-dipping')
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopted an independent approach for hypothesis testing to ensure that data used to define the ROIs were not related to the hypothesis testing data, in line with the principles of null hypothesis testing (Kriegeskorte et al. 2009).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use independent ROI definitions or independent localizer data; explicitly state measures taken to avoid circularity and cite Kriegeskorte when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROI signal extraction and statistical testing
rubrics_metrics.description: For each participant the mean signal across all voxels was extracted for contrasts Spont Laugh > NV and Conver Laugh > NV from each ROI; analyses included 3 (ROIs) × 2 (Contrasts) × 2 (Groups) ANOVA and follow-up tests per ROI, with post hoc analyses reporting F, t, p, means, and effect sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe extraction method (mean across voxels), statistical model (ANOVA with ROI × contrast × group), and report follow-up/post-hoc tests with appropriate statistics and effect sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavioral statistical modeling with mixed effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Linear mixed model analysis using lme4 with Laughter Type and Group as fixed effects and participants and word items as crossed random effects; model term selection guided by AIC; significance established using Satterthwaite’s method; emmeans used for Tukey HSD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model both subject- and item-level random effects; use AIC to guide model selection; use appropriate packages to obtain t-statistics and p-values (car, lmerTest) and report estimated marginal means with multiple comparisons correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vigilance/attention monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Vigilance trials involved a 0.5-s beep sound requiring participants to press a button within 3 s; five vigilance trials per run were included to assess attentiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include occasional attention checks during passive tasks and report adherence; use vigilance trials to exclude inattentive participants if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling and reporting of exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Two autistic males were unable to complete the scan due to discomfort and health concerns; after exclusions the scan groups remained comparable for sex, age, verbal, performance, and full-scale IQ but still differed on AQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report reasons for exclusions, re-run group comparability tests after exclusions, and report resulting sample sizes (N scanned vs N recruited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stimulus counterbalancing and reuse constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Sound stimuli were used twice each across the experiment; trial conditions were pseudorandomized to prevent >2 consecutive trials of the same condition; pairs were pseudorandomized and counterbalanced across runs and participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reusing stimuli, ensure counterbalancing so each stimulus appears equally across conditions and participants; document pseudorandomization algorithms and constraints to prevent order effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed reporting of behavioral result metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Behavioral analyses reported fixed effects estimates, CI, p-values, random effects (σ2, τ00), ICC, N participants, N words, observations, AIC, and marginal/conditional R2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide comprehensive tables for mixed-model outputs including both fixed and random effects, model-fit indices, and relevant summary statistics for transparency and reproducibility.
